front: Main stages in processing an ore
back: Crushing and grinding → concentration (froth flotation) → roasting/smelting → refining.
Concentrating finely ground ore: mineral particles stick to air bubbles and float in a froth; waste rock sinks.

front: What does roasting a sulfide ore do?
back: Heats it in air, turning sulfides into oxides and releasing sulfur dioxide.
Impure copper anode; pure copper cathode; acidified copper(II) sulfate electrolyte.
Unreactive metals (silver, gold, platinum) that fall from the anode during refining; a valuable by-product.

front: How is gold recovered in large mines?
back: Dilute sodium cyanide (with air) dissolves the gold; it is recovered on activated carbon or by displacement with zinc.

front: Why is mercury dangerous in gold mining?
back: Its vapour is poisonous; it pollutes rivers and builds up in fish.
Processing a raw material into a product that is worth more.
Processing minerals in the country where they are mined instead of exporting raw ore.
Jobs, skills, higher export earnings, new local industries and tax revenue.
notes: Challenges: electricity, investment, skills and pollution control.
